decisions.reason: It is close to the firm's sewer, utility and fabricated metal capabilities, so management would likely give this adjacent product time to build demand.
Public waste bins use similar metalworking and coating assets but sit furthest from the firm's core fluid-handling offer, making them the likeliest line to be cut in a refocus on core business.
Ground sleeves are a sensible extension of standard fabricated infrastructure components and fit the firm's aim to broaden adjacent markets.
The cast-iron variant is somewhat less aligned with the firm's steel and stainless strengths, but it still complements the ground-sleeve range and would usually be kept unless volumes disappoint.
This steel variant matches the firm's established processing expertise very well and is therefore likely to remain in the portfolio.
